quote: The Supply Agreement replaces this with: "Customer shall purchase from Supplier, and Supplier shall be Customer's exclusive source of, all glass and PET containers for any beverage product manufactured, filled, bottled or packaged by or for Customer or its Affiliates, worldwide." (Supply Agreement § 3.1) ... Harrowgate cannot buy a single PET water bottle, a wine container, or a container for a facility in, say, Mexico or the UK without breaching the Agreement. ... [Additional Observation A:] Supply Agreement § 15.1 (Entire Agreement) expressly supersedes all prior term sheets. The Term Sheet therefore has no direct legal effect.
reason: Issue 2 identifies the right provision (§ 3.1) and its scope: all glass and PET containers, any beverage, worldwide. It contrasts this with the term sheet's agreed scope of amber glass bottles for beer brands at U.S. and Canadian facilities. It explains the consequence: Harrowgate is in breach if it buys elsewhere, and breach supports termination. Observation A confirms that the entire-agreement clause supersedes the term sheet, so Harrowgate is bound by the broader executed text. The memo also recommends narrowing § 3.1 back to the agreed scope.
